s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic swelling and pain over the clavicular area with a tender mass and elevated inflammatory markers
salient_findings: 6-month history of swelling and moderate pain over the left clavicular area
Tender 2 × 3 cm swelling over the left clavicle with erythema
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 50 mm/h
key_facts: No fever, weight loss, or trauma
Tender swelling over the left clavicle
Small clean overlying wound and erythema
Normal complete blood count, renal and liver function tests
Midclavicular lytic expansile lesion with a minimally displaced pathologic fracture on chest radiograph

shortlist.label: Osteomyelitis of the clavicle
shortlist.why_kept: Tender swelling and elevated inflammatory markers

shortlist.label: Ewing sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Lytic expansile lesion with a minimally displaced pathologic fracture

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Lytic lesion and elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate

shortlist.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Lytic expansile lesion with a minimally displaced pathologic fracture

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Lytic lesion and tender swelling over the clavicle

raw.rationale: The presence of a midclavicular lytic expansile lesion with a minimally displaced pathologic fracture, along with an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and a 6-month history of swelling and pain, is most consistent with Ewing sarcoma, a malignant bone tumor that can cause such radiographic and clinical findings.

rejected.label: Osteomyelitis of the clavicle
rejected.why: The absence of fever, normal complete blood count, and lack of discharge or significant infection signs make osteomyelitis less likely.

rejected.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
rejected.why: While Langerhans cell histiocytosis can cause lytic bone lesions, the clinical presentation and the specific radiographic findings are more suggestive of a malignant process like Ewing sarcoma.

rejected.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
rejected.why: Aneurysmal bone cysts are typically benign and may not fully account for the systemic symptoms like an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate or the aggressive nature of the lesion described.

rejected.label: Eosinophilic granuloma
rejected.why: Eosinophilic granuloma, part of Langerhans cell histiocytosis, usually presents with solitary bone lesions and might not fully explain the extent of the clinical and radiographic findings in this case.
